gloss: river, stream; flow, stream (to); shine, be radiant; light
summary: The root's commonest word is נָהָר, a river or stream of running water: the river out of Eden, the Nile and its canals, the rivers of Babylon, and above all “the River”, the Euphrates, the bound of the land promised to Abram “from the river of Egypt to the great river” (Gen 15:18). Its verb is to flow or stream, used of peoples who “stream” to the mountain of Yahweh's house in the last days (Isa 2:2; Mic 4:1); a second verb of the same spelling is to shine, be radiant, of faces that look to Yahweh (Psa 34:6), with the noun נְהָרָה “daylight” (Job 3:4) and the Aramaic light that dwells with God (Dan 2:22). Arabic keeps the same two sides in one root, nahr “river”, nahara “flow” and nahār “day, daylight”.

words.summary: About 120 times. A river of running water, in the plural also the streams or arms of a great river (Egypt's canals, Exo 7:19). With the article and no name, הַנָּהָר is the Euphrates, as Gen 15:18 and Jos 1:4 spell out. The plural is both נְהָרוֹת and נְהָרִים; the dual stands in the place name אֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם, “Aram of the two rivers”.

senses.definition: A stream of running water in its channel: one that waters a garden and divides into four heads, the named rivers of a land, and their waters that rise, overflow and can be dried up.

evidence.note: “וְנָהָר goes out from Eden to water the garden, and from there it divided and became four heads.”
The second and third rivers, Gihon and Hiddekel, and the fourth, פְרָת.
“Are not Abanah and Pharpar, נַהֲרוֹת דַּמֶּשֶׂק, better than all the waters of Israel? May I not wash in them?”
Over the waters of Egypt, “over their נַהֲרֹת, over their channels and over their pools”: the arms and canals of the Nile.
“The waters will fail from the sea, וְנָהָר will be dried up and become dry”: a river is what can run dry.
Egypt “rises like the Nile, and like the rivers (כַנְּהָרוֹת) its waters toss”.
Among the exiles “by נְהַר־כְּבָר”, the river Chebar.
“עַל נַהֲרוֹת בָּבֶל, there we sat, yes, we wept.”
“If a river (נָהָר) presses on him, he is not alarmed.”
The Peshitta: they were baptised by John “in the river (בּנַהרָא) Jordan” (ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ, with ποταμῷ in many copies).

senses.definition: With the article and no name, the great river of Mesopotamia: the bound of the land promised to Abram, the line beyond which Israel's fathers served other gods, and, in the Persian books, the province “Beyond the River”.

evidence.note: “From the river of Egypt to הַנָּהָר הַגָּדֹל נְהַר־פְּרָת”: the River is named as the Euphrates.
“As far as the great river, the river Euphrates.”
“From the wilderness to הַנָּהָר.”
“Your fathers dwelt of old בְּעֵבֶר הַנָּהָר, Terah … and they served other gods.”
Solomon ruled “from the River to the land of the Philistines”.
Yahweh will shave with a razor hired “in the regions beyond the River, with the king of Assyria”.
“He shall have dominion from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.”
The governors of עֵבֶר הַנָּהָר, the Persian province west of the Euphrates.
The sixth bowl is poured on “the great river, the Euphrates” (τὸν ποταμὸν τὸν μέγαν τὸν Εὐφράτην; the Peshitta נַהרָא), and its water is dried up.

senses.gloss: river, as a figure of abundance and of overwhelming force
senses.definition: A river's ceaseless flow as a picture of peace and glory given in fullness, and its flood as a picture of overwhelming trouble or an invading army.

evidence.note: “Then your peace would have been כַנָּהָר, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.”
“Behold, I extend peace to her כְּנָהָר, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream.”
“נָהָר, its channels make glad the city of God.”
Yahweh brings on them “the waters of the River, mighty and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory”.
“When you pass through the waters I will be with you, וּבַנְּהָרוֹת they will not overflow you.”
“Many waters cannot quench love, וּנְהָרוֹת will not drown it.”
“נָשְׂאוּ נְהָרוֹת, Yahweh, the rivers have lifted up their voice.”
“Out of his belly shall flow rivers (ποταμοί; the Peshitta נַהרַוָתָֿא) of living water.”
“A river (ποταμόν; the Peshitta נַהרָא) of water of life, bright as crystal, going out from the throne of God and of the Lamb.”

parallels.note: Sea and river side by side, the two great waters.
The waters, set beside the rivers.
The Nile and its streams beside the rivers of Egypt.

phrases.gloss: beyond the River: the land east of the Euphrates (Jos 24), or in the Persian books the province west of it
the river of Egypt, the south-west bound of the land promised to Abram
Aram of the two rivers, Mesopotamia

evidence.locator: Gen.2.10, וְנָהָר → ποταμὸς; Gen.15.18; ποταμός renders נָהָר ×97, with ποταμοί, ποταμοῖς, ποταμούς ×10

evidence.note: “The great river, the Euphrates”, the Hebrew's הַנָּהָר הַגָּדֹל נְהַר־פְּרָת (Gen 15:18).
The four angels bound “at the great river Euphrates”.
The river of water of life out of the throne of God.

words.gloss: river; (Beyond the River) the province west of the Euphrates
words.summary: The Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra: once the river of fire before the Ancient of Days, and otherwise only in עֲבַר נַהֲרָה, the Persian province Beyond the River. The word עֲבַר of that phrase is in the avar entry. The BDB key also takes the Hebrew construct נְהַר (Gen 15:18 and others), counted here by spelling.

senses.definition: A river; of the stream of fire that flows out from before the Ancient of Days at the judgment.

evidence.note: “נְהַר דִּי־נוּר was flowing and going out from before him.”

senses.definition: In עֲבַר נַהֲרָה, the River is the Euphrates and the phrase the Persian province west of it, Samaria and Judah among it.

evidence.note: The nations settled “in the city of Samaria and the rest of עֲבַר־נַהֲרָה”.
Tattenai, “governor of עֲבַר־נַהֲרָה”.
The cost to be paid “from the tribute of עֲבַר נַהֲרָה”.
Artaxerxes' decree to “all the treasurers who are in עֲבַר נַהֲרָה”.

words.summary: Three or four times, always of peoples streaming to a place as a river flows: to the mountain of Yahweh's house in the last days, and no more to Bel in Babylon. BDB files the six qal tokens under both this verb and נָהַר “shine” (n.br.aa); the verses are divided here by sense.

senses.definition: Of nations and peoples coming in a continual stream to one place, like a river to its outlet.

evidence.note: “The mountain of the house of Yahweh shall be established at the head of the mountains … וְנָהֲרוּ אֵלָיו כָּל־הַגּוֹיִם”; the next verse, “many peoples will go and say, Come, let us go up”.
The same prophecy: “וְנָהֲרוּ עָלָיו עַמִּים.”
“I will bring out of his mouth what he has swallowed, וְלֹא־יִנְהֲרוּ אֵלָיו עוֹד גּוֹיִם; the wall of Babylon has fallen.”
“They will come and sing on the height of Zion, וְנָהֲרוּ אֶל־טוּב יְהוָה, to the grain, the new wine and the oil”: streaming to Zion as in Isa 2:2, though “be radiant” (Isa 60:5) is also possible.

words.summary: Twice in the Hebrew, of a face that brightens with joy at what it sees. It shares its spelling with “stream” (above), and BDB files the same six tokens under both.

senses.definition: Of the face, to light up at the sight of deliverance, the opposite of a face covered with shame.

evidence.note: “הִבִּיטוּ אֵלָיו וְנָהָרוּ, and their faces shall not be ashamed”: radiance set against shame.
“Then you will see וְנָהַרְתְּ, and your heart will fear and be enlarged”, after “Arise, shine (אוֹרִי), for your light has come” (Isa 60:1).
“The eyes of your heart being enlightened (πεφωτισμένους; the Peshitta ונֵנהרָנ)”.

words.summary: Once, in Job's curse on his day. One use only, but its verb, the Aramaic נְהוֹר and the Arabic nahār “daylight” agree.

senses.definition: The light that shines on a day, which Job wishes withheld from the day of his birth so that it should be darkness.

evidence.note: “That day, let it be darkness (חֹשֶׁךְ) … וְאַל־תּוֹפַע עָלָיו נְהָרָה”: the opposite of darkness, shining on a day.
“The moon will not give its light (φέγγος).”

words.gloss: cleft, channel in the rock (hiding place)
words.summary: Once, plural, of hiding places Israel made in the mountains from Midian, beside caves and strongholds. BDB files it under “shine” as dubious; Arabic manhar, a place hollowed out by running water and a channel through which water runs, ties it instead to the river sense. One use only, so its exact sense rests on that cognate and its setting among caves.

senses.gloss: cleft, water-cut channel used for hiding
senses.definition: Places in the mountains, named with caves and strongholds, which Israel made ready to hide in from Midian: most likely clefts or channels cut in the rock by water.

evidence.note: “The sons of Israel made for themselves אֶת־הַמִּנְהָרוֹת which are in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.”

words.summary: Daniel's word for the light that is with God, read נְהוֹרָא (the written text נהירא). BDB's key also lists Dan 5:11, 14, which are נַהִירוּ (below).

senses.definition: Light, as what dwells with God, set against the darkness whose hidden things he knows.

evidence.note: “He reveals the deep and hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, וּנְהוֹרָא עִמֵּהּ שְׁרֵא.”

words.summary: Twice, in the queen's and Belshazzar's praise of Daniel: light of the mind, listed with understanding and wisdom.

senses.definition: Light of understanding: the power to see into hidden things, found in Daniel with understanding and wisdom.

evidence.note: “In the days of your father נַהִירוּ וְשָׂכְלְתָנוּ וְחָכְמָה, like the wisdom of the gods, were found in him.”
Belshazzar repeats it: “נַהִירוּ and understanding and excellent wisdom are found in you.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's river, for ποταμός: the Jordan, the Euphrates, the rivers of living water and the river of water of life.

senses.definition: A river of running water, and in figure the floods that beat on a house and the living water that flows from the believer and from the throne of God.

evidence.note: Baptised by John “בּנַהרָא, the Jordan”.
“On the sabbath day we went out of the city to the side of the river (נַהרָא).”
“The rain came down and the rivers (נַהרַוָתָֿא) came.”
“Rivers (נַהרַוָתָֿא) of living water will flow from his belly.”
“On the great river (נַהרָא) Euphrates.”
“A river (נַהרָא) of living water, clear as crystal, going out from the throne of God and of the Lamb.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's common word for light (φῶς), some seventy times: daylight, a lamp's light, and the light that Jesus and his disciples are.

senses.definition: Light, the opposite of darkness: of the world, of a lamp, and of the word and life of God shining in men.

evidence.note: “The people sitting in darkness saw a great light (נֻוהרָא)”, quoting Isa 9:1.
“You are the light (נֻוהרֵה) of the world.”
“The life was the light (נֻוהרָא) of men, and the light shines (מַנהַר) in the darkness, and the darkness did not overtake it.”
“I am the light (נֻוהרֵה) of the world.”
“God is light (נֻוהרָא), and in him is no darkness at all.”

senses.definition: Lit up, shining, of a body or cloud full of light, and of the lights of heaven.

evidence.note: “If your eye is single, your whole body will be נַהִיר.”
“A bright (נַהִירתָּא) cloud overshadowed them.”
“You shine among them as lights (נַהִירֵא) in the world.”
“The bright (נַהִירָא) morning star.”

senses.definition: With clear sight, of the blind man healed.

evidence.note: “He was restored and saw everything clearly (נַהִירָאיִתֿ)” (τηλαυγῶς).

words.summary: The Peshitta's verb for shining and giving light (λάμπω, φωτίζω, φαίνω): the peal is to shine, the aphel to give light or to shine, the pael to enlighten, the ethpaal to shine forth.

senses.definition: To shine, of a face, of the righteous, of disciples' light before men, and of the earth lit by a messenger's glory.

evidence.note: “So let your light (נֻוהרכֻֿון) shine (נֵנהַר) before men.”
“Then the righteous will shine (נֵנהרֻון) like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.”
“His face shone (וַנהַר) like the sun.”
“The earth was lit (נֵהרַתֿ) by his glory.”

senses.definition: To give light to others or to a place, of a lamp, of the true light that lights every man, and of the glory of God that lights the city.

evidence.note: A lamp on its stand “gives light (ומַנהַר) to all who are in the house”.
“The true light, which gives light (דּמַנהַר) to every man, coming into the world.”
“To give light (למַנהָרֻו) to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death.”
“The city has no need of the sun … for the glory of God gave it light (אַנהַרתָֿה), and its lamp is the Lamb.”
“The Lord God gives them light (מַנהַר).”
“Until the day dawns (נַנהַר) and the morning star rises in your hearts.”

senses.definition: To make all men see, bringing a hidden purpose into the light.

evidence.note: “And to enlighten (וֵאנַהַר) all, what is the administration of the mystery hidden from the ages in God.”

senses.definition: To shine out, of the light God commanded to shine out of darkness.

evidence.note: “God who said that light should shine (דּנֵתֿנַהַר) out of darkness has shone in our hearts.”

cognates.gloss: (nahr) a channel in which water runs; a river, rivulet, canal; (nahara) it (water) ran along the ground and made itself a channel; it flowed
cognates.note: The river and the flowing of its water: the noun נָהָר and the verb “stream”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2858, art. نهر, نَهْرٌ (n40633)
evidence.note: “A channel in which water runs … or the water itself [that runs therein; i. e., a river; a rivulet; a brook; a canal of running water].”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2857, art. نهر, نَهَرَ (n40631)
evidence.note: “It (water) ran upon, or along, the ground, and made for itself a نَهْر … It ran, or flowed.”

cognates.gloss: day, daytime; broad daylight; the light between dawn and sunset
cognates.note: In the same Arabic root as nahr “river”: the light of day, as Hebrew נְהָרָה and the verb “shine”. Lane also gives نَهَرٌ “light and amplitude” and نَهَارٌ أَنْهَرُ “a bright day”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2858, art. نهر, نَهَارٌ (n40636)
evidence.note: “Day; or day-time; contr. of لَيْلٌ: or broad daylight … the light between the rising of the dawn and sunset.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2858, art. نهر, نَهَارٌ أَنْهَرُ (n40639)
evidence.note: “A bright day.”

cognates.gloss: the place of a river; a place the water hollows out in a river's channel; a cleft or hole through a fortress wall by which water runs
cognates.note: The same pattern as מִנְהָרָה (prefix m-, place of): a cleft cut by water, which fits the hiding places named with caves in Jdg 6:2.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2858, art. نهر, مَنْهَرٌ (n40640)
evidence.note: “The place of a river. A place which the water hollows out in a نَهْر. A cleft, or hole, in a fortress, passing through [the wall], whence water runs.”

cognates.note: Akkadian has lost the h. Its nūru “light” is of another root (that of נֵר), not this one.
Jewish Aramaic, in the Targums for the Hebrew נָהָר (Targ. Gen 2:10; Jon 2:4) and in the Talmud of canals.

evidence.locator: N00282, נְהַר II (נַהֲרָא I, נַהֲרָה), Targ. Jon. II, 4; Targ. Gen. II, 10

cognates.gloss: shine; (passive participle) bright, clear; (pael, aphel) give light, illumine
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: the Targum of Psa 34:6 uses the ithpeel “be brightened” for the Hebrew וְנָהָרוּ.

evidence.locator: N00280, נְהַר I, Targ. O. Gen. XLIV, 3; Targ. Job XVIII, 5; Pa. Targ. O. Gen. I, 15; Ithpe. Targ. Ps. XXXIV, 6

cognates.note: Listed in the Proto-Semitic root set but not yet found in Dillmann or Leslau.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh cut a covenant with Abram: “To your seed I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates” (Gen 15:18), and Moses and Joshua repeat the bound (Exo 23:31; Deu 11:24; Jos 1:4). Solomon ruled over the kings from the River to the border of Egypt (1Ki 5:1, 4), but Abraham himself was given “not even a foot's breadth” of it, though God promised to give it to him and to his seed after him (Act 7:5), and he died in faith “not having received the promises” (Heb 11:13). The psalm of the king's reign looks for a dominion “from the River to the ends of the earth” (Psa 72:8), and Zechariah gives the same words to the king who comes riding on an ass (Zec 9:9–10). From the verses: the land between the rivers was promised to Abraham himself as well as to his seed, he has not yet received it, and it is to be given when the king of Zechariah's prophecy reigns.

Isaiah and Micah say that “in the last days” the mountain of the house of Yahweh will be established at the head of the mountains, “and all the nations will stream (וְנָהֲרוּ) to it”, saying “Come, let us go up to the mountain of Yahweh … for out of Zion goes forth the law, and the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem”, and he will judge between nations and they will beat their swords into ploughshares (Isa 2:2–4; Mic 4:1–3). Jeremiah uses the same verb of Babylon: the nations “will not stream to him any more” (Jer 51:44). From the verses: the nations' streaming is a movement on earth, to a mountain in Jerusalem, at a time when war has not yet ceased among them; it turns from Babylon to Zion, and it describes the kingdom Yahweh will set up there, not a heaven beyond the earth.

note: BDB files the same six qal tokens under both n.bq.aa (flow) and n.br.aa (shine); they are divided here by sense (flow: Isa 2:2, Mic 4:1, Jer 51:44, Jer 31:12; shine: Psa 34:6, Isa 60:5), but lexicon-support counts six uses for each. Jer 31:12 could be either: placed under flow for its likeness to Isa 2:2 (coming to Zion). Whether “flow” and “shine” are one root: Arabic keeps nahr “river” and nahār “daylight” in one root, which argues they belong together, but how is not shown; Wiktionary calls the Hebrew shine verb a loan from Aramaic. The Aramaic xn.ad.ac also takes the Hebrew construct נְהַר of Gen 15:18 etc. by spelling. xn.ad.ad (נְהִיר) and xn.ad.ae (נְהִירוּ) both resolve to Dan 5:11, 14 in the database; Dan 2:22 (Qere נְהוֹרָא) is the verse for נְהִיר. מִנְהָרָה: m.cm.al is a zero-token cross-reference to n.br.ac, not named. Peshitta: SEDRA roots 1144 NHR (shine: lexemes 1915 NHYRA, 1916 NHYRAYT, 1917 NHR, 1918 NWHRA) and 1145 NHR (1919 NHRA river); Syriac verb stems from SEDRA's form codes (Eph 3:9 pael, 2Co 4:6 ethpaal). Ugaritic nhr (ṯpṭ nhr, Judge River, title of Yam in the Baal cycle, KTU 1.2) not yet cited from DULAT. Ge'ez nahār not found in Dillmann. No personal names are formed from the root (Nahor and Naharai are נחר); אֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם is a place name, kept as a phrase. The phrase עֲבַר נַהֲרָה's first word is in avar.
